title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: COP27 outcomes in Egypt
sections.summary: COP27 in Egypt produced decisions reaffirming commitment to limit warming to 1.5°C, adapt to impacts and increase support for developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 27th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP27) held in Egypt last year was set against challenging global geopolitical and economic conditions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite this, countries were able to deliver a package of decisions that reaffirmed their commitment to limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, adapt to the unavoidable impacts of climate change and increase support for finance, technology and capacity building for developing countries.

sections.label: 2030 NDC emissions reduction decision
sections.summary: It asks how the decision was reached to reduce emissions to around 60 MTCO2 in the revised 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How was the decision reached to reduce emissions to around 60 MTCO2 in our revised 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)?

sections.label: Public sector net-zero lead
sections.summary: The public sector has committed to taking the lead in achieving net-zero emissions around 2045.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The public sector has committed to taking the lead of achieving net-zero emissions around 2045.

sections.label: Industry and energy emissions share
sections.summary: In 2021, the industrial and energy sectors together contributed 88% of Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2021, the industrial sector and energy sector collectively contributed to 88% of Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions.

sections.label: Supporting workers in green transition
sections.summary: It asks how the Government will support workers affected by the green transition and what training, education and green business initiatives exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, as we transition to become a green economy, new jobs and business opportunities will be created in almost every sector, ranging from engineering to finance, manufacturing to trade, services to construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Workers and staff who are unable to adapt will risk unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How will the Government support workers who will be affected by the green transition?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Government share an update on the training and education measures to facilitate the preparation of workers for good jobs and career paths in this nascent sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What initiatives are available to promote and support green businesses to encourage Singaporeans to explore such new opportunities?

sections.label: Revised climate targets announced
sections.summary: After public consultation, climate targets were revised to reduce emissions to around 60 million tonnes CO2 equivalent in 2030 and reach net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In October, after several months of public consultation, we formally revised our climate targets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will reduce our emissions to around 60 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2030, after peaking our emissions earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We also committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

sections.label: Public sector net-zero 2045
sections.summary: The public sector will aim for net-zero emissions around 2045, five years ahead of the national 2050 target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The public sector will set the example by aiming to achieve net-zero emissions around 2045, five years ahead of our national target of 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax levels
sections.summary: The Government has specified carbon tax levels up to 2027 and a range of $50 to $80 per tonne of CO2 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Government has specified carbon tax levels up to 2027 and a range of $50 to $80 per tonne of CO2 by 2030.

sections.label: Greener production and growth sectors
sections.summary: Beyond economy-wide moves, sectors will be helped to reorient towards greener production and develop competitive advantages in growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Aside from economy-wide moves, such as carbon tax and decarbonising our grid, we will also help sectors reorient towards greener production and develop competitive advantages in growth sectors.

sections.label: Businesses and SME sustainability
sections.summary: Every business, including SMEs, must be financially and environmentally sustainable by decarbonising value chains and accelerating green transition, with MTI reporting on SME help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Every business, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), must be financially and environmentally sustainable in order to thrive in the long run, by decarbonising their value chains and accelerating their green transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: MTI will report on how we are helping SMEs to level up in areas, such as sustainability reporting and carbon accounting.

sections.label: Eco-stewards and green skills
sections.summary: MOE will elaborate on nurturing young eco-stewards with a focus on food sustainability in 2023, and Singaporeans will be supported in green skills and jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) will elaborate on how we will nurture our young to become eco-stewards and live sustainably, with a focus on food sustainability in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will also support Singaporeans to acquire green skills and improve their access to green job opportunities.

sections.label: Forward Singapore social compact
sections.summary: The Government has embarked on the Forward Singapore exercise to refresh and renew the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Government has embarked on the Forward Singapore exercise to refresh and renew our social compact.

sections.label: Singapore ageing population and Japan study
sections.summary: Singapore's population ages rapidly with low birth rate and longer life expectancies, and a 2021 Japan study shows ageing and decline harm economies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's population continues to age rapidly, with low birth rate and longer life expectancies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to a recent study in 2021 on the long-term projections of economic growth in 47 prefectures of Japan, Japan's population's aging and decline has catastrophic impacts on the national and subnational economies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In its most pessimistic modelling, with zero immigration growth and without significant improvement in productivities, Japan's GDP can decline to levels back in the 1970s.

sections.label: Budget is pro-family
sections.summary: A speaker states that one of the biggest takeaways from this Budget is that it is pro-family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, one of the biggest takeaways from this Budget is that it is pro-family.

sections.label: Singapore total fertility rate decline
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate fell from above five in 1960 to around replacement level by the mid-1970s and stayed below since.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's total fertility rate (TFR) declined from above five in 1960 to around replacement level by the mid-1970s and has remained below replacement level since.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the past trend of TFR, the growth of Singapore Citizen workforce will slow down and its size will be expected to shrink at some point.

sections.label: COVID-19 work-from-home experiment
sections.summary: COVID-19 let business and public sectors test productive work from home, with evidence of better retention, job satisfaction and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, COVID-19 has quite unexpectedly enabled the business sector and public sector to conduct a natural experiment to test whether work can be productively done when most employees are working from home.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is some evidence that WFH, whereby employees work a mix of days at home and at the workplace each week, improves firms' retention rates and workers' job satisfaction and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is also striking that preferences for WFH arrangements are stronger among women with children.

sections.label: Policies to boost total fertility rate
sections.summary: Existing measures to boost total fertility rate remain important, and the speaker asks what systems-wide approach can ride on the work-from-home momentum.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the slew of policy measures already in place to boost total fertility rate, including parental leave, childcare subsidy, child tax reliefs and the Baby Bonus remain important, what systems-wide approach can be taken to ride on the momentum of the aforementioned natural experiment to facilitate the achievement of our citizens' career goals and satisfying family life with children?

sections.label: Request for more paternity leave
sections.summary: The speaker asks for more, specifically 12 more weeks of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As we celebrate this good news, and I do not want to sound too greedy, we need to ask for more, 12 more weeks of paternity leave.

sections.label: Equalising leave roadmap request
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will commit to equalising leaves and announce a roadmap for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will the Government commit to this and announce a roadmap for equalising the leaves?

sections.label: Citizens' workgroup on childcare sick leave
sections.summary: Asks whether the PMO will form a citizens' workgroup on childcare sick leave recommendations addressing parents and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will PMO form a citizens' workgroup to look into recommendations about childcare sick leave that will address both the concerns of working parents and businesses?

sections.label: Gender neutral fertility leave proposal
sections.summary: States the Government can do more to help employers be sympathetic by introducing gender neutral fertility leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As we create a Singapore made for families, the Government can do more to help employers be more sympathetic by introducing gender neutral fertility leave.

sections.label: Implementing and legislating FWA guidelines
sections.summary: Asks whether the tripartite guidelines on FWAs can be implemented this year and considered for legislation instead of guidelines only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can we implement the tripartite guidelines on FWAs this year and also consider legislating the guidelines instead of having them only as guidelines?

sections.label: Singapore TFR decline
sections.summary: States Singapore's TFR declined from a 1988 high of 1.96 to 1.1 in 2021 and 1.12 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After hitting a recent high of 1.96 in 1988, Singapore's TFR has been steadily on the decline, down to new lows of 1.1 and 1.12 in 20 21 and 2022 respectively.

sections.label: Female caregivers outside labour force
sections.summary: States that of caregivers outside the labour force, 89% were females, based on MOM's 2022 report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on the Ministry of Manpower (MOM)'s Labour Force in Singapore 2022 Report of caregivers who are outside the labour force, a dominant 89% were females.

sections.label: Parental leave flexibility increased
sections.summary: The firm is extending parental leave, giving primary caregivers 26 weeks fully paid and secondary caregivers six weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The firm is extending and increasing the flexibility of parental leave with all parents benefiting from 26 weeks of fully paid leave for primary caregivers and six weeks for secondary caregivers.

sections.label: First Step Grant increase
sections.summary: The Budget Statement announced an increase in the First Step Grant from $3,500 to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget Statement, it was announced that there would be an increase in the First Step Grant from $3,500 to $5,000.

sections.label: Infant formula tin price
sections.summary: A Straits Times report says a 1.8kg tin of infant milk formula can cost as high as $113.35.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a recent report in The Straits Times, the price of a tin of infant milk formula can go as high as $113.35 for a 1.8kg tin.

sections.label: KOM prosecution and CPIB
sections.summary: The US prosecuted KOM and fined it US$422 million, but CPIB reportedly found insufficient evidence to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The US succeeded in prosecuting KOM and imposed a huge fine of US$422 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But we were told CPIB is unable to find sufficient evidence to prosecute.

sections.label: Mutual legal assistance request responses
sections.summary: She said she does not know all MLA details but at least one or two latest requests had no response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When asked about the mutual legal assistance (MLA) requests, she replied that she does not know all the details of the MLA but that for at least one or two of the latest ones there were no response.

sections.label: New citizen and PR numbers
sections.summary: Minister Indranee said 2020 and 2021 new citizen and PR numbers were impacted by COVID-19 measures; the question asks about 2022.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply debate in the last two years, Minister Indranee mentioned that the numbers of new citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs) granted in 2020 and 2021 were impacted by COVID‐19‐related travel restrictions and safe management measures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: What were the numbers of new citizens and PRs granted in 2022 and were these numbers still impacted by COVID‐19?

sections.label: Digital government services progress
sections.summary: Singapore has pursued e-government since the early 1980s and asks about progress of Smart Nation and Digital Government efforts and citizen benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Government services are therefore very much part of our everyday life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Building on a strong foundation of efficiency, our Government has been on the e‐Government journey since the early 1980s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Today, our Government has achieved much and won international acclaim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: From e‐government then to digital government today, we should continue our efforts to make Government services more convenient, user‐friendly and at a lower cost for our citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this vein, I would like to ask, what is the current progress of the “Smart Nation and Digital Government” efforts and how have citizens and businesses benefited from these efforts?

sections.label: Critical information infrastructure cyber threats
sections.summary: Singapore's critical information infrastructure is a prime target, and the Ministry is asked what threats were detected and stopped in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We are therefore a prime target, especially our critical information infrastructure (CII).

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should focus on operational technology security, and it becomes ever more important and urgent for us to do so, to shelter our CII from increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Ministry, what threats have been detected and stopped during the past year?

sections.label: SNDGG technology projects rolled out
sections.summary: SNDGG rolled out projects including a personal alert button, lift monitoring, drowning detection, and technologies like LifeSG, PayNow and Digital IC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: SNDGG has rolled out many projects to test technologies such as the personal alert button to help the elderly seek help, the lift monitoring system in Town Councils, the computer vision drowning detection and also develop technologies that we are now regularly using such as Life SG, PayNow and Digital IC.

sections.label: Malaysia and Japan voting age
sections.summary: Malaysia in 2019 and Japan in 2016 lowered their voting age to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, these two countries have also lowered their voting age to 18, Malaysia in 2019 and Japan in 2016.

sections.label: Capital punishment for young offenders
sections.summary: A young person above 18 who commits a capital crime is liable to capital punishment and hanging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As far as taking significant personal responsibility where actions is concerned, today, if a young person above 18 commits a capital crime, he is liable to suffer capital punishment and be hanged.

sections.label: Public declaration of interests mechanism
sections.summary: The passage notes existing prohibitions and codes, and asks whether the Prime Minister's Office will consider a public declaration system, citing the EU Transparency Register.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the Parliamentary Act 1962 prohibits the over exchange of gifts and fees for influence in Parliament and civil servants are governed by a Code of Conduct which articulates key conduct principle and expected behaviour, the lack of public knowledge of how different interest groups are advanced and handled can lead to misunderstandings or speculations that damage the trust and standing of our elected officials and public institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Prime Minister Office consider a mechanism to create and administer a public system of declaration for these purposes?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Taking the EU Transparency Register as an example, the ideas to open about what interests are being pursued, by whom and with what budgets?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It requires that all organisations and interest groups that seek to influence directly or indirectly, policy-making EU institutions including elected officials are registered on the Transparency Register and need to follow a code of conduct.

sections.label: Islandwide vending machine deployment
sections.summary: Josephine Teo said 1,600 islandwide vending machines distributed 30 million masks, 1.3 million TraceTogether tokens and 2.5 million ART kits with automatic ID verification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As Minister Josephine Teo shared at last year’s Committee of Supply, the deployment of islandwide 1,600 vending machines enabled the distribution of 30 million masks, 1.3 million TraceTogether tokens and 2.5 million ART kits with automatic ID verification.

sections.label: Centralised platform and personalised services
sections.summary: Centralising functions on one platform would improve citizen experience and help the Public Service aggregate data and use AI to push integrated services matching individual needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The centralisation of different functions on a single platform would enhance the user experience of our citizens and make it easier for the Public Service to aggregate data and utilise AI to "push" integrated services from across different Government agencies to match an individual’s specific needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How is the Public Service enhancing how we serve citizens better, including providing more personalised services centeon people’s needs through technology, especially seniors and how is the Public Service planning to better partner people and private sector to stay agile and resilient?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This month marks a major victory in our fight against COVID-19 as we stepped down from DORSCON Yellow to Green.

sections.label: Public Service agility and officer skills
sections.summary: The pandemic showed the importance of Public Service agility and cross-deployability, as officers were redeployed and trained for the National Call Centre for Mask Collection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has emphasised the importance of the agility of the Public Service, especially through enhancing officer’s cross-deployability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For example, the National Call Centre for Mask Collection was stood up quickly by re-deploying many Public Service officers to the call centres to support the mask distribution efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: These officers were not frontline service staff and had to be trained quickly to manage calls and address queries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It also underscores the importance of developing a Public Service with officers equipped with multiple, diverse and future-ready skillsets that we can tap on quickly to address critical needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On behalf of our unions and union leaders in the public sector, I wish to ask how is the Government supporting the growth and development of public officers so that officers can acquire diverse skills, and to ensure that Public Service remains ready, relevant and resilient – ready with the new skills, relevant to the new jobs and requirements, and resilient to the new changes and curveballs hurled at us?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, five years ago, I spoke in this House about the $422 million price settlement for Keppel Offshore & Marine (KOM) for bribery acts in Brazil conducted through its subsidiary in the United States.

sections.label: CPIB warnings to former KOM executives
sections.summary: In January 2023 CPIB issued stern warnings to six unnamed former KOM senior executives, though no one was charged despite about $55 million paid in bribes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Almost five years later, in January 2023, CPBI issued stern warnings to six unnamed former KOM senior executives for the same corruption case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What is difficult to understand for many Singaporeans is that while the company has admitted liability and paid massive fines, the CPIB could not find a single person working in the company whom they could charge for complicity in the bribery acts even though about $55 million of KOM's monies were paid out for bribes.

sections.label: SPH circulation numbers inflated
sections.summary: Executives at Singapore Press Holdings, now SPH Media Trust, inflated circulation numbers by up to 90,000 daily copies, including by printing and destroying extra copies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Then, there are other recent cases where aspects of corporate or investment governance involving our GLCs have some under question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We learnt that executives at Singapore Press Holdings, now SPH Media Trust, inflated circulation numbers by up to 90,000 daily copies, including by printing and destroying extra copies of newspapers.

sections.label: Temasek exposure to Adnani Group
sections.summary: Press reports indicated that Temasek may be exposed to companies under the Adnani Group, possibly to the tune of several billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Recently, press reports indicated that Temasek may be exposed to companies under the Adnani Group, possibly to the tune of several billion dollars.

sections.label: CPIB Director corruption investigation powers
sections.summary: The Director of CPIB has powers under the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960 to investigate corruption, so it can happen here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: From a jurisdictional perspective though, it can happen here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is because the Director of CPIB is vested with the powers under the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960 (PCA) to investigate corruption.

sections.label: CPIB reopening PCA review
sections.summary: The speaker says there is scope for CPIB to reopen the review of the PCA that it closed in October last year without taking any step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, it is my respectful view that there is scope for the CPIB to reopen the review of the PCA that it closed in October last year without taking any step.

sections.label: AGC conditional warning to KOM
sections.summary: In 2017, the AGC served KOM a conditional warning in lieu of prosecution under the PCA, requiring payment of more than $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2017, the AGC served KOM with a conditional warning in lieu of prosecution for an offence under the PCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In lieu of prosecution, KOM had to pay more than $100 million to the Singapore authorities.

sections.label: Extending PCA to foreign bribery
sections.summary: The speaker says it makes sense to extend the ambit of the PCA to cover foreign bribery committed by a Singapore company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In these circumstances, it makes sense to extend the ambit of PCA to cover situations where acts of foreign bribery were committed by a Singapore company.

sections.label: Resident TFR historic low
sections.summary: In 2022, the resident total fertility rate reached a new historic low of 1.05.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2022, our resident TFR reached a new historic low of 1.05.

sections.label: Life expectancy and ageing
sections.summary: Resident life expectancy at birth rose from about 72 years in 1980 to more than 83 years today, and by 2030 about one in four citizens will be 65 or above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Resident life expectancy at birth has risen from about 72 years in 1980 to more than 83 years today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: By 2030, about one in four Singapore citizens will be aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Transnational and inter-ethnic marriages
sections.summary: Around one in three citizen marriages each year were transnational and around one in six were inter-ethnic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In recent years, around one in three citizen marriages each year were transnational and around one in six, inter-ethnic.

sections.label: BTO priority for families
sections.summary: First-timer families with children and younger married couples get greater priority in BTO flat applications, including an additional ballot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First-timer families with children as well as younger married couples will receive greater priority in their BTO flat applications, including an additional ballot.

sections.label: Increased financial support for parents
sections.summary: Financial support for raising a child is increased through higher Baby Bonus Cash Gift, CDA First Step Grant and CDA co-matching cap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are increasing financial support for the early years of raising a child where it is most needed by parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have increased the Baby Bonus Cash Gift and the Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant for all eligible Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, we have raised the CDA Government co-matching cap for the first and second child.

sections.label: Financial support amounts per child
sections.summary: Parents can receive up to $24,000 for their first child and up to $37,000 for subsequent children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With these enhancements, parents can now receive up to $24,000 in financial support for their first child and up to $37,000 for their subsequent children.

sections.label: Doubled Government-paid Paternity Leave
sections.summary: Government-paid Paternity Leave will double for eligible working fathers of children born on or after 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced in Budget, we will double Government-paid Paternity Leave for eligible working fathers of children born on or after 1 January 2024 onwards, something that Mr Louis Ng had long asked for.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs
sections.summary: Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs will be rolled out in 2024, requiring employers to fairly and properly consider FWA requests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To further encourage the adoption of FWAs, we will roll out the Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs in 2024, which will require employers to fairly and properly consider FWA requests.

sections.label: Guidelines on Singapore Women's Development
sections.summary: Tripartite partners are developing the guidelines' scope, and the Guidelines will be introduced by 2024 as committed in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Tripartite partners are developing the scope of the guidelines and we should also give them enough time to consult stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will thus introduce the Guidelines by 2024, as committed in the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

sections.label: Child Development Account uses
sections.summary: Mr Faisal Manap asked about expanding approved Child Development Account uses, and the Baby Bonus Cash Gift was just enhanced by $3,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about expanding the approved uses of the Child Development Account to purchase items such as infant formula and diapers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have just enhanced the Baby Bonus Cash Gift by $3,000.

sections.label: CPF cash top-up tax relief
sections.summary: A tax relief of up to $8,000 per calendar year is provided to individuals who make a cash top-up to loved ones' CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, we also provide a tax relief of up to $8,000 per calendar year to individuals who make a cash top-up to their loved ones' CPF savings.

sections.label: Fair hiring and TAFEP guidelines
sections.summary: Qualifying salaries were raised, COMPASS was introduced, TAFEP protects workers from discriminatory hiring, and TAFEP guidelines will be enshrined into law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We fully understand Singaporeans' concerns about job competition and we remain committed to ensuring that Singaporeans can compete fairly and strongly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have raised qualifying salaries over the years and introduced the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) protects workers from discriminatory hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will be enshrining the TAFEP guidelines into law.

sections.label: Immigration numbers in 2022
sections.summary: Since the late 2009 tightening, immigration has been measured and stable, with about 23,100 new citizenships and 34,500 new PRs granted in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since the tightening of our immigration framework in late 2009, we have maintained a measured and stable pace of immigration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2022, we granted about 23,100 new citizenships, including about 1,300 to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also granted about 34,500 new Permanent Residencies (PRs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The numbers of new citizenships and PRs granted in 2022 were slightly higher than pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Factors for PR and citizenship
sections.summary: PR or citizenship is granted based on factors including family ties to Singaporeans, economic contributions, qualifications, family profile, age and length of stay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: When granting PR or citizenship, we look at a comprehensive set of factors, including an individual's family ties to Singaporeans, economic contributions, qualifications, family profile, age and how long they have stayed in Singapore.

sections.label: Population planning parameter scenarios
sections.summary: Various scenarios are used instead of a single population planning parameter, and the 6.9 million parameter remains relevant for the 2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As such, we do not plan on a single population planning parameter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Instead, increasingly we develop various scenarios to stress-test our assumptions and allow for a range of possible outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2018, we provided an update that our total population is likely to be significantly below 6.9 million by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Based on the various scenarios we have, this remains the case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The planning parameter of 6.9 million remains relevant for the 2030s.

sections.label: Singpass and PayNow usage
sections.summary: 4.2 million people use the Singpass app, and over 300 million transactions were made on PayNow in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singpass and PayNow are widely used – 4.2 million people use the Singpass app today, and over 300 million individual and corporate transactions were made on PayNow in 2022.

sections.label: GoBusiness grants and satisfaction
sections.summary: GoBusiness suggested grants that Abundance used, and citizen and business satisfaction with government services improved from 2016 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The GoBusiness portal also suggested suitable grants, such as the Productivity Solutions Grant and Energy Efficiency Grant, which Abundance used to improve its operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These efforts have helped improve citizen satisfaction with government services from 73% in 2016 to 84% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Business satisfaction with government services has also improved from 64% to 79%.

sections.label: ScamShield launch and blocking
sections.summary: ScamShield launched on iOS in 2020 and Android in 2022, has about 500,000 users, and has blocked scam calls and detected scam messages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, ScamShield was launched on iOS in 2020 and on Android in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It has about 500,000 users and since 2022, has helped block 200,000 scam calls and detected over 3.5 million scam messages.

sections.label: Government systems migration progress
sections.summary: 64% of eligible government systems have been migrated, with a target of 70% by this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To date, we have migrated 64% of eligible government systems, and we are on track to hit our target of 70% by this year.

sections.label: AI Singapore business partnerships
sections.summary: Since 2017, AI Singapore has partnered around 80 businesses, created close to $60 million of value, and supported Q&M Dental Group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2017, AI Singapore has partnered around 80 businesses to co-develop AI models and solutions, and created close to $60 million of value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, it supported Q&M Dental Group to develop an AI model that helps dentists detect disease from dental X-rays and recommend treatment plans.

sections.label: AI apprentices training doubled
sections.summary: AI Singapore will double AI apprentices trained over the next five years from 200 to 400.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To meet strong demand from both industry and Singaporeans, AI Singapore will double the number of AI apprentices trained over the next five years from 200 to 400.

sections.label: Government cybersecurity operations centre launched
sections.summary: The Government launched a Cyber Security Operations Centre to use artificial intelligence and data analytics in defending government systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government will step up our proactive cybersecurity measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have launched the Government Cyber Security Operations Centre to make greater use of artificial intelligence and data analytics in defending government systems.

sections.label: Jurong Lake District innovation challenge
sections.summary: SNDGO and URA, with IMDA support, rolled out an Innovation Challenge in Jurong Lake District focusing on urban sustainability issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am pleased to announce that SNDGO and URA, with support from IMDA, have just rolled out an Innovation Challenge in Jurong Lake District today, focusing on urban sustainability issues.

sections.label: Corruption offences Penal Code placement
sections.summary: CPIB assesses there is no compelling need to site corruption-related Penal Code offences within the PCA, as its officers have requisite powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With regard to Mr Murali's suggestion that corruption-related Penal Code offences be sited within the PCA, CPIB's assessment is that there is currently no compelling need to do so, as CPIB officers possess the requisite powers to investigate offences under the Penal Code.

sections.label: PCA extra-territorial application for citizens
sections.summary: The PCA applies extra-territorially to Singapore Citizens, and CPIB can act regardless of whether corrupt acts occurred in Singapore or abroad.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Where these individuals are Singapore Citizens, the PCA is currently of extra-territorial application.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The CPIB is empowered to take action against them irrespective of whether they committed the corrupt acts in Singapore or abroad.

sections.label: Non-conviction-based confiscation mechanism review
sections.summary: MHA and CPIB will review the non-conviction-based confiscation mechanism further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and CPIB will review the non-conviction-based confiscation mechanism further.

sections.label: Confidential investigation process and evidence
sections.summary: The investigation process and evidence obtained during investigations are confidential.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The investigation process and the evidence obtained in the course of investigations, is confidential.

sections.label: CPIB investigation of six individuals
sections.summary: CPIB investigated offences under the PCA, looked into six individuals and the KOM and KCL boards, found only the six involved, but lacked sufficient evidence to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And my reply, which still applies, is that CPIB investigates offences under the PCA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, there is no doubt on this, what I can share is that CPIB did look into the six individuals and the boards of KOM as well as their parent entity Keppel Corporation Limited (KCL).

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: CPIB's investigations established the involvement of the six individuals, and no one else was implicated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the case of the six individuals, CPIB did not have sufficient evidence to justify prosecution to prove a case beyond reasonable doubt for the reasons I have already explained.

sections.label: Three MLA requests to Brazil
sections.summary: AGC and CPIB sent three MLA requests to Brazil to secure needed evidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If you look at the record, what I had said on the MLA was that AGC and CPIB had sent three MLA requests to Brazil to secure evidence that was needed.

sections.label: Evidentiary burden and unavailable testimony
sections.summary: They could not meet the evidentiary burden for proof beyond reasonable doubt, and crucial evidence and oral testimony were unavailable in Singapore and could not be compelled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What they were not able to do was that they could not cross the evidentiary burden that they feel or they had been advised is necessary in law, in order to make out the case beyond a reasonable doubt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it is not that CPIB could not find people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And as I explained in my earlier reply, the bulk of the evidence and the oral testimony which is crucial is not available in Singapore and we cannot compel the people to come here.

sections.label: Keppel follow-up under DPA
sections.summary: Keppel had followed up as a result of the Deferred Prosecution Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the case of Keppel, I understand that they had followed up as a result of the Deferred Prosecution Agreement (DPA).

sections.label: Anti-Corruption Partnership Network established
sections.summary: The Anti-Corruption Partnership Network was established in 2018 to encourage the private sector to take ownership of preventing corruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For example, the Anti-Corruption Partnership Network (ACPN) was established in 2018 to encourage the private sector to take ownership of the need to prevent corruption.

sections.label: Lowering voting age suggestion
sections.summary: Both sides have raised lowering the voting age; previous considerations remain valid, and other countries' reasons do not apply here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Both sides of the House have previously raised this suggestion and our previous considerations remain valid.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A number of countries have lowered their voting age – some to increase voter turnout, and others, perhaps for perceived political advantage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We do not have the first problem and we certainly should not do it for the second reason.

sections.label: Conflicts of interest management
sections.summary: Thanking Ms He Ting Ru for comments on managing potential conflicts of interest in the Public Service and among MPs, a three-pronged approach is adopted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Next, we thank Ms He Ting Ru for her comments on how we should not be complacent in the management of potential conflicts of interests both in the Public Service and amongst elected Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We adopt a three-pronged approach to safeguard ourselves.

sections.label: SGUnited public officer redeployment
sections.summary: Under SGUnited, more than 4,000 public officers were redeployed to fight COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Under SGUnited, more than 4,000 public officers were redeployed to fight COVID-19.

sections.label: Centralised surge manpower structure
sections.summary: The pandemic showed the need for a centralised system to redeploy surge manpower; the Public Service Division will set up a structure, building on SARS-era measures like NPHL.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, the pandemic underscored the importance of having a centralised system to identify and redeploy surge manpower across agencies to quickly support critical crisis functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As we emerge from the pandemic, the Public Service Division will systematically set up a structure to do this so that we are better prepared for future crises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore could react quickly when COVID-19 emerged as we had the benefit of learning from our SARS experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We strengthened our emergency preparedness following SARS and established key public health institutions, including the National Public Health Laboratory (NPHL) which was set up in 2009.

sections.label: Population figure not a target
sections.summary: The figure is not a target but a planning parameter, and it is not a target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first thing I want to clarify, and I hope that everybody in the Chamber will pay attention to is, that the figure is not a target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is a planning parameter and it keeps coming up every time people ask the question, "Is 6.9 million a target?" or "Is the other figure a target?" It is not a target.

sections.label: Figure is a planning guideline
sections.summary: People may think of it as a target, but it is a guideline along which planning is done, not something to achieve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think that subliminally and subconsciously people think of it that way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I really do hope that people understand that it is a guideline, along which we plan; not something that we set out to achieve.

sections.label: Unanswered awareness questions on corruption payments
sections.summary: Two questions remain unanswered: whether the board of directors and six KOM executives were aware of and authorised the corrupt payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Having said that, there were still two questions that I believe remains unanswered to this day, which is that whether the board of directors at the time when the corruption payments were made, were they aware of the act and also whether the six KOM executives were aware of and authorised the corrupt payments.

sections.label: CPIB investigation into Keppel case
sections.summary: CPIB investigated whether corruption was committed and who committed it, looking into six individuals and the boards of KOM and Keppel Corporation Limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And what I explained earlier in response, was that, when CPIB is investigating the Keppel case, they are looking to see whether corruption has been committed, and if so, who's committing it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I also said – she may not have heard the answer – I said, what I can share is that CPIB looked into the six individuals and the boards of KOM as well as their parent entity Keppel Corporation Limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And after looking into all of that, the investigations established the involvement of the six individuals.

sections.label: Investigation agencies narrowed to six individuals
sections.summary: Investigation agencies looked at corporations and individuals, narrowed it to six individuals, and felt there was reason to issue a stern warning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And they are only supposed to investigate offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the short answer is: they have looked at the corporations, they have looked at individuals and they have narrowed it down to these six individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The investigations are carried out by the investigation agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But the investigation agencies obviously felt that there was reason enough to issue a stern warning.

sections.label: Actions against employees before Deferred Prosecution Agreement
sections.summary: Actions against employees were done before 2018 and the DPA, with some terminated and some counselled, and KOM required an extensive corporate ethics and governance programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Leong may not be aware, because he was not a Member of this House in 2018 when I answered it, but actually, the bulk of what he has asked about what the company did and actions taken against the employees were, in fact, done prior to 2018 before they entered into the Deferred Prosecution Agreement (DPA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I would ask the Member to read the Hansard and secondly, to also read the DPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Some employees were terminated, some were put on counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, please check the DPA, but there were definitely actions and steps taken against the employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And as part of the DPA, in order to arrive at that agreement, the US Attorney's Office and the US Department of Justice required a very extensive corporate ethics and governance programme, which KOM was required to comply with before the charges would be withdrawn.
